method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name, RTTI name and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of twelve natives that the earlier contracts do not record: the nameplate natives _setNameplate and _setNameplateVisible, the actor identity natives _getStaticActorID and _isExistActor, the area natives _setInstanceRaid and _getZoneName, the item natives _bindSpreadSheetData and _countStack, the package query _getItemPackageFreeSpace, and the group natives _countMember, _isMember and _getGroup. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish nameplate content, actor existence rules, item data, group membership or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/scheduler_item_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/spreadsheet_native_call_contract.json framework, manifests/widget_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/talk_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling through 0x00D19A20, the holder receiver adapter, the invalid-parameter route, the return pushers, the world object chain and the item package lookup.

typeRegistry.order: The constructor stores the StackOperator vftables 0x0110DF38, 0x0110DF60, 0x0110DF88, 0x0110DFB0, 0x0110DFD8, 0x0110E000, 0x0110E028, 0x0110E050, 0x0110E078 and 0x0110E0A0 as entries 0 to 9. Their RTTI names are int, float, bool, Utf8String, LuaControl*, AutoReleaseTentative, Nil, Table, IndividualIndex and Variable.

registration.note: GroupBase has a second vftable at 0x00FD53AC whose slot 2 is 0x006DD180. The order of a native is its position among the rel32 calls of its switchboard, counted from 1, as in the scheduler contract.
registration.globalNote: The Global switchboard registers the script level natives _defineClass and _defineBaseClass next to _isExistActor, so the Global class is the receiver of the receiverless names. manifests/boot_native_call_contract.json records the global_u descriptor with the selector global for _getStaticActor. The script index lists no descriptor for _isExistActor. Only _isExistActor has a contract in this record. The registrar addresses were read from the name literal reference inside each registrar.

holders.reused: 0x00726510 and 0x00726460 (CharaBase), 0x00726300 (ActorBase) and 0x00726670 (ItemBase) are recorded in manifests/scheduler_item_native_call_contract.json framework.holders.
holders.note: The invoke routines cast the receiver with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl (0x01270B4C) to the target type descriptor. A null cast returns false without calling the callback. The qualifier letter of the holder RTTI name tells const (BEX) from non-const (AEX).

argumentReaders.0x0071BB80: Reads cell tag 4, a LuaControl*, and casts a non-null control to ActorBase with the type descriptor 0x01270964. A null pointer passes. A failed cast or another tag reaches 0x00CCA730. It returns the address of the cell holder.
argumentReaders.0x0071C080: The same reader with the type descriptor 0x012C2308, which is SpreadSheet.
argumentReaders.0x0071CD90: Bounds-tests an index against the cell vector and reads the cell through 0x0071C2A0. That reader accepts tag 8, an IndividualIndex, and returns the address of two dwords.
argumentReaders.0x00581AE0: Bounds-tests an index against the cell vector and reads the cell through 0x005819A0.

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. X = [R] and Y = [X +0x04]. The same chain as the scheduler contract.

fields.Y +0x0E0: Object that _setNameplate hands the listener to through 0x0076FF20.
fields.Y +0x118: Sheet binding manager that _bindSpreadSheetData calls through 0x00767120.
fields.Y +0x12C: Object queried through 0x007646D0 by the 0xFF path of _bindSpreadSheetData.

framework.invalidParameterRoute: A failed cell vector size test calls 0x009D22B4. The target cursor contract records that routine as the invalid-parameter route that ends in TerminateProcess.

arguments.note: Nameplate slot number n. The callback uses n - 1 to address a record and does not test the range.
Actor the nameplate describes. The reader casts a non-null control to ActorBase. A null control pointer passes.
Value stored in the slot record and handed to the listener.
Trailing values. The callback reads the cells from index 3 and keeps ints, Utf8Strings and controls.

rows.behavior: Reads the slot number, an actor control, an int and the trailing values. It writes the actor identity, the int and a copy of the trailing values into the slot record of the receiver, builds a SetNameplateMessageListener and hands it to the object at world field +0xE0 together with the receiver. The listener runs at once when the byte at +0x59 of the object at receiver +0x60 is nonzero and is queued otherwise. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument list builder makes four entries. Registry entries 0, 4, 0 and 9 give int, LuaControl*, int and Variable.
Cell 0 and cell 2 are read through 0x005819A0 and cell 1 through 0x0071BB80. Three cell vector size tests call 0x009D22B4 on failure.

0x0071BB80 accepts only a tag 4 cell. A null control pointer returns the cell holder. A non-null pointer is cast with 0x009DA6CC from LuaControl to the type descriptor 0x01270964, which is ActorBase. A failed cast and a tag other than 4, which includes Nil, reach 0x00CCA730.

The callback first computes n minus 1 (add esi,-1 at 0x006F5F9C), so n is 1-based. It addresses the record at the receiver plus 0x68 plus 0x38 times (n minus 1), which is receiver plus 0x38 times n plus 0x30. It stores the identity that 0x00CC73B0 returns for the control at record +0x00 and the third argument at +0x04. No test bounds n. The value 0 addresses receiver +0x30, one record before slot 1, and whether that is in range was not traced.

0x007702C0 builds a parameter record from the cells at index 3 onward. A tag 0 cell is read through 0x005819A0, a tag 3 cell through 0x0071CE70 and a tag 4 cell through 0x0071BEB0. A control is passed to virtual slot 0x84 of its vftable through 0x006DBF90. Any other tag is skipped.

The callback copies the parameter record into the slot record at receiver +0x30 + 0x38 * n through 0x004D5900, which assigns the container, and copies the dwords at +0x14 to +0x24 and the byte at +0x28. With the identity and int stores this makes a 0x38 byte record at receiver +0x30 + 0x38 * n.

A 0x48 byte object is allocated through 0x009D1B35 and constructed by 0x00744C10. Its vftable 0x00FD76C8 has the RTTI name SetNameplateMessageListener nested in CharaBase. The constructor stores the engine dword at +0x04, the receiver identity at +0x08, the actor identity at +0x0C, the int at +0x10 and n at +0x14. It copies the parameter record into +0x18 through 0x007446E0.

The object that the listener goes to is the dword at +0xE0 of Y, with Y the dword at +0x04 of [R] and R the address that 0x00CC7510 returns. The callback calls 0x0076FF20 on it with the receiver and the listener.

0x0076FF20 reads the dword at receiver +0x60. A nonzero byte at +0x59 of that object calls virtual slot 1 of the listener with the object and then destroys the listener through slot 0. A zero byte converts the receiver control to an identity through 0x00CC73B0, with the manager as the handle, and passes the key, the identity, a zero and the listener to 0x0076FD80. The listener is not destroyed on that path. The key is the first dword of the object, or 0 when that dword is -1.

Listener slot 1 (0x00744E70) allocates a 0x10 byte object through 0x00744D60 and calls 0x00771C20 on the dword at +0xDC of Y with the engine handle, that object, the actor identity, the int and the parameter record.
The callback never calls the yield request 0x00CD2860 and never touches the return container. It ends with ret 4.

The listener belongs to the display name resolver. Its base vftable 0x00FD40E4 has the RTTI name GetNameListenerInterface nested in DisplayNameResolver, and the byte at +0x59 reads as a name ready flag. The roles come from those names.
The body of 0x0076FD80, the object that 0x00771C20 runs on, the capacity of the slot table behind the receiver and the meaning of the second int.

rows.callbackKind: thin adapter into a body routine

returns.note: True when the engine knows the name in a loaded state and the object behind it carries a nonzero flag byte.

rows.behavior: Reads one Utf8String and asks the engine name table three questions in turn. The name must be present with a state in the loaded set. The name must resolve to a handle. The handle must reach an object whose byte at +0x7D is nonzero. A failed question pushes false. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds an empty adapter through 0x0078BB90 and calls the body 0x0078CB90 with ExecuteParameters.
The body reads the Utf8String at cell 0 through 0x0071CE70 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure.

0x00CC7200 runs 0x00CD9C60 on the engine implementation, which looks the name up through 0x00CD8870 with the create flag 0. An absent name returns false. A present name returns the result of 0x00CE16C0, which is true when the dword at entry +0x08 equals one of the dwords at 0x0130D4FC, 0x0130D500 and 0x0130D504.
The three dwords hold 0x00010008, 0x00010009 and 0x0001000A in the file image of .data.

0x00CC7A00 looks the name up again through 0x00CD8870 with the flag 1 and returns the first dword of the entry, or 0 for a miss. 0x00CC72A0 resolves that handle through 0x00CD7A30, which returns 0 for a zero handle, and returns the byte at node +0x7D without a null test.
With the flag 1, a miss in both tables of 0x00CD8870 calls 0x00CD5320 on the dword at engine implementation +0x1CC with the name.
The first question has found the name, so the second lookup does not miss and the flag 1 branch is not reached. A concurrent removal was not considered.
The result is pushed through 0x00748870 at either exit of the body.
The loaded set and the flag byte read as an actor that exists in the world. The names of the three state dwords and of the byte at +0x7D come from the native name.
The classes behind the engine name tables, the meaning of the three state dwords and how a Lua script reaches a Global native, because the receiver of a global call was not traced.

arguments.note: Sheet control. The reader casts a non-null control to SpreadSheet.

rows.behavior: Reads a SpreadSheet control and looks up the item record of the ItemBase reference. When the catalog id of the record lies inside a key range of the sheet it records the id and requests the row through the sheet binding manager of the world object. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument is read at cell 0 through 0x0071C080 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure. The reader accepts only a tag 4 cell and casts a non-null control with 0x009DA6CC to the type descriptor 0x012C2308, which is SpreadSheet.
The callback compares the dword at ItemBase +0x68 with the dword at 0x00FE0508, which is 0x000000FF. Equal goes to 0x006F5400 and unequal to 0x006F5380. Neither path reads the byte at +0x70.

The unequal path finds the record with 0x006EE480 on the package manager and reads the catalog id at record +0x24. 0x006DFFC0 tests the id against the key range pairs of the sheet. A true result inserts the id into the set at package manager +0x54 through 0x007213F0 and calls 0x00767120 on the dword at +0x118 of Y with the engine handle, the id and the sheet.

The equal path finds the record with 0x006EE3E0 and reads the same id. A true range test looks up the dword pair at record +0x10 and +0x14 in 0x007646D0 on the dword at +0x12C of Y, inserts the id into the set held by the object that returns through 0x007213F0 without a null test, and calls 0x00767120 as above.
0x006DFFC0 calls slot 14 (+0x38) of the handle at sheet +0xB4 for the key vector and scans it as pairs of a start key and a count. It does not test the handle for null.

0x00767120 inserts the sheet pointer into the set at manager +0x04 through 0x00781F00. A new entry runs 0x006DECC0 on the sheet with the manager. It then calls 0x006F0D80, the row request of the SpreadSheet contracts.
Neither path tests the result of the record lookup, so an absent record reads the address 0x00000024.
The native asks the sheet for the row of the item catalog id so the name and data reads find it cached. The role comes from the native name and the row request call.
The class of the manager at +0x118 of Y and of the object at +0x12C, and the meaning of the dword pair at record +0x10 and +0x14.

returns.note: Count of zero dwords in the package slot vector, or 0 for an absent package.

rows.behavior: Reads a 1-based package number, finds the package record of the receiver and pushes the number of zero dwords in the dword vector at record +0x14. An absent package pushes 0. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback builds a helper object through 0x006DD450 and calls 0x007027E0 with ExecuteParameters and the receiver.

0x007027E0 reads the package number at cell 0 through 0x005819A0 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure, subtracts 1 through 0x0078BC90 and finds the package through 0x006F51A0 and 0x006E5BA0.
A null package pushes the int 0 through 0x00584F70. Otherwise 0x006E5A90 counts the zero dwords between record +0x14 and +0x18 and the count is pushed.
The zero dwords are the free slots of the package. The role comes from the native name.

arguments.note: Member to find. A control is read through 0x0071BB80 as an ActorBase. An IndividualIndex is read through 0x0071CD90.
Optional 1-based position. A Nil cell skips the position test.

returns.note: True when the member is in the group and, if a position is given, sits at that position.

rows.behavior: Resolves the member to an index in the group through 0x006C3560. A tag other than 4 or 8, or a negative index, pushes false. With a Nil second argument a found member pushes true. Otherwise it pushes whether the index equals the second argument minus 1. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The argument list builder 0x00743020 makes two entries. Entry 0 is a Which built by 0x00740970 over registry entries 4 and 8, which are LuaControl* and IndividualIndex. Entry 1 is registry entry 0, an int.
The callback tests the cell vector at 0x006FFF14 and dispatches on the tag byte of cell 0. Tag 4 goes to 0x006FFFBB, tag 8 to 0x006FFF32 and any other tag sets the result to false at 0x00700025.
A tag 4 cell is read through 0x0071BB80, converted to an identity through 0x00CC73B0 and looked up with 0x006C3560 on the address of receiver +0x68. An index below 0 gives false.

A tag 8 cell is read as two dwords through 0x0071CD90. The lookup uses a handle built from the second dword. When it returns a negative index and the first dword is nonzero, a handle built from the first dword is tried.

The result starts true. A tag 6 byte in cell 1 keeps it. Otherwise cell 1 is read through 0x00581AE0 and the result is whether the index equals that int minus 1. A second size test requires at least two cells.
The marshaller supplies a tag 6 placeholder when Lua passes one argument, so the position test is optional for a Lua caller.
The index is the position in the group member list. The role comes from the native name.
The body of the lookup behind 0x006C3560 and 0x006C3320, and the handle class built by 0x00CC9320.

returns.note: GroupBase control, or nil when the group is not valid.

rows.behavior: Reads one int and asks the group manager of the world object for the group of the receiver identity and that int. A valid group becomes a GroupBase control that is pushed. An invalid group pushes nil. It requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback calls the shared helper 0x00701140 with ExecuteParameters and the flag 0. The sibling _getExtendedTemporaryGroup calls the same helper with the flag 1.
The helper reads the int at cell 0 through 0x005819A0 after a cell vector size test that calls 0x009D22B4 on failure.
It calls 0x006C4560 on the dword at +0xE4 of Y with the receiver identity address and the int, and tests the result with 0x006CB950. A failed test pushes nil through 0x00748920.

A valid result calls 0x006E2240 and pushes the control through 0x00748B30. 0x006E2240 creates the control through 0x00CC80A0 for the flag 0 or 0x00CC8140 otherwise with the immediate argument 0x012BFB65, casts it to GroupBase with the type descriptor 0x012C07E8 and copies 16 bytes of the group handle to control +0x68. 0x012BFB65 is an unaligned .data address, not a hash or an id.
The bytes at control +0x68 are the group reference that _countMember and _isMember read. The link is the common offset and the GroupBase cast.
The role of the .data argument 0x012BFB65, the group manager at +0xE4 of Y and the meaning of the int.

A client that implements them still needs the nameplate presentation behind the listener, the engine name tables, the area string and flag writers, the item and sheet data and the group manager, which this record does not supply.

nextTranche.basis: Distinct scripts that contain a call, taken from xivl-client-scripts:lua/napi_index.json, with the call-site count as the tie break. Natives with a contract in any manifest are excluded, except that a registration-only row of manifests/desktop_native_call_contract.json with declared lists and no traced callback counts as uncovered (_addItem, rank 1). boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order in the framework.
Script call-site lines are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time.
The nameplate listener, the display name resolver queue behind 0x0076FD80 and the presentation object behind 0x00771C20 were not traced, so what a nameplate shows is not established.
The engine name tables behind 0x00CD8870 and the meaning of their state dwords were not traced, so which names _isExistActor accepts is not established.
How a Lua script reaches a Global native, the receiver of a global call, was not traced.
The group manager, the group handle class and the sheet binding manager were not identified.

The invalid-parameter route ends in a process terminate on the evidence of the target cursor contract. The record lookups without a null test and the unchecked nameplate slot number were not run, so their run-time effect is unknown.
These are client marshalling and state contracts. They do not establish nameplate content, item data, group membership or server behavior.
